source.title: Skewness risk and the cross-section of cryptocurrency returns

hypothesis: Cryptocurrencies with lower lagged return asymmetry risk earn higher subsequent weekly returns; a weekly long-low-skew/short-high-skew portfolio should therefore have positive net alpha.
universe: Point-in-time Binance USD-M USDT perpetuals. Each Monday retain the top 50 contracts by lagged trailing-30-day quote volume among assets with exact daily history and a valid skewness estimate.
feature: Negative rolling skewness of daily close-to-close returns over W prior completed UTC days. Higher signal means lower realized skewness/asymmetry risk.
signal_direction: Long lowest-skewness quintile / short highest-skewness quintile.
portfolio: Equal-weight market-neutral long/short, 0.5 gross per side.
execution: Feature and liquidity inputs end Sunday; rebalance Monday 00:00 UTC open and hold to next Monday open.
development_gate: Canonical mean rank IC of -skewness >0.02 with HAC p<0.05, positive low-minus-high skewness return spread, canonical net Sharpe >0.70 and total return >0, and at least 2/3 windows positive after costs.
success_gate: Canonical OOS net Sharpe >1.0; OOS rank IC >0.02; positive at 2x costs; at least 2/3 windows positive; 2024 and 2025 non-negative; max drawdown <35%; excluding BTC/ETH positive; excluding strongest contributor positive; DSR reported.
source_deviation: The paper's asymmetry-risk construction emphasizes idiosyncratic skewness. This first-order adaptation uses causal rolling total-return skewness because a clean point-in-time residual-skew implementation would introduce an additional model specification. If rejected, OOS is preserved where the development gate fails.
